plan: [In this second-price auction, bidding my true value is weakly dominant: I win whenever the second-highest bid is below my value and I never pay more than the prize is worth to me. [In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding my true private value is a dominant strategy and maximizes expected profit. There is no prior history to exploit; overbidding risks winning and paying more than my value. With value $6, I will bid 6.0 to maximize long-run payoff.]

[My value is $0. In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, payoff = value − second-highest bid, so winning with positive payment gives negative payoff. To maximize expected profit (and avoid losses this round), bid my true value: $0. Bidding 0 avoids paying anything; ties could win at price 0 (zero payoff) but never a loss.]
